source.verbatim_statement: Let (1) be a consistent system of inequalities and let \(F_n\) and \(F_m\) each satisfy (3). Then there exists a constant \(c>0\) such that for any \(x\) there exists a solution \(x_0\) of (1) with \(F_n(x-x_0)\) at most \(cF_m((Ax-b)^+)\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the public-domain scan of Hoffman (1952), Section 2, The Main Theorem, page 263; mathematical symbols were linearized in the transcription field.

proposed_definition_changes.reason: The former handle named influence functions and cross-fitting without defining its terminal indicators, backward regressions, censoring hazards, longitudinal scores, ratio score, fold construction, or simultaneous rectangle.  The corrected construction exposes every one of those objects and the Hall-feasible projection used for nonempty inversion.

proposed_assumptions.reason: Uniformly shrinking positive inference needs fixed quantitative assignment, survival, and censoring overlap plus explicit cross-fitted nuisance and product-rate control; pointwise positivity in the base model does not imply any of them.
proposed_assumptions.standard_or_novel: standard: quantitative longitudinal AIPW overlap and cross-fitting regularity (BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023)
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This condition does not assume coverage, contraction, or optimizer recovery.  It only controls information and second-order nuisance remainders, and the theorem derives all inferential and decision conclusions from those primitive rate conditions.

proposed.comparator_claim: Assumption 1 supplies the published uncapped residual no-carry-over equality, Proposition 1 supplies threshold-wise scalar bounds, and the decision section compares deterministic switching regimes.

The paper formulates factual-arm sequential coarsening at random and develops influence-function and multiply robust estimation for its recurrent-event mean and survival functionals; it does not state identification of the entire sustained-history law or the finite vector used here.
The paper characterizes atom-sensitive sharp bounds for the distribution of an unrestricted sum with fixed marginals.

Theorem 4 characterizes nonempty fixed-margin staircase transportation classes by critical-position inequalities, and Section 3 gives constructions; Theorem 1 is the general arbitrary-pattern support antecedent.
The paper gives greedy optimization results for staircase transportation problems with structured rewards.
The paper shows that the joint geometry of partially identified treatment payoffs governs minimax-regret rules and their randomization.
The paper formulates compatibility of causal marginal models with a single global structural causal model.
The paper obtains confidence regions for identified sets by inverting criterion functions under moment equalities and inequalities.
The paper develops regularized support-function inference for polygonal affine identified sets with changing active faces.

prose_updates.tldr: A randomized recurrent-event trial identifies separately capped baseline and residual margins while leaving their dependence unknown, and the raw recurrent paths remain unbounded. The externally prespecified sensitivity restriction \(B+W\le H\) creates a Ferrers transport problem and is not implied by separate capping. The cap-fibre response-tree construction proves every feasible triple coupling attainable, including in the published raw no-carry-over subclass. Exact endpoints and the common-law value polytope yield deterministic and randomized minimax regret and the cap-three recommendation reversal. For inference, a direct sequential-factorization proof now identifies every supported sustained-history atom and hence \((r_{bt},q_w)\); on the explicit quantitative-overlap and cross-fitted product-rate submodel, a longitudinal AIPW Bonferroni rectangle contracts at root-\(n\) rate and its perspective inversion covers the whole value set and every deterministic or randomized robust optimizer, including ties. On the broader pointwise-overlap class \(\mathfrak M_H\), uniformly shrinking inference remains impossible by the vanishing-information two-law construction. Thus the positive quantitative theorem and the negative base-class theorem have disjoint, explicit scopes.

project_justification.gap: The closest recurrent-event switching analysis supplies an uncapped no-carry-over equality, scalar sharp bounds, and deterministic decision criteria. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supplies the factual-arm sequential-CAR setup and influence-function architecture for recurrent-event mean and survival targets, but not an atom-by-atom identification theorem for the complete sustained history, the capped margin vector used here, shared-law deterministic and randomized regret inversion, or the positive-versus-negative uniform-inference boundary. Dahl2008 supplies staircase feasibility only.
project_justification.fill: The formal kernel combines the attributed staircase feasibility certificate with an explicit raw-path cap-fibre lift, derives the complete common-law value and regret geometry, and proves the missing inference chain. Sequential CAR and positivity give a finite product of observed transition kernels for every supported absorbing history atom. Explicit backward regressions, cumulative censoring hazards, longitudinal AIPW and ratio influence functions, cross-fitting, Hall-feasible projection, and conservative simultaneous inversion give root-\(n\) value-set and regret-excess contraction on a quantitative regularity submodel. A separate two-law theorem proves that pointwise positivity in the unchanged base class cannot yield uniform shrinkage.

sampling_model.overlap: The maintained class assumes positive baseline assignment and positive arm-specific factual censoring continuation on every supported at-risk history, with no positivity for the unsupported switch. The positive inference submodel separately fixes \(H\), \(K\), and \(\varepsilon>0\) and requires assignment, landmark survival, and every supported factual continuation probability to be at least \(\varepsilon\); the base class itself is unchanged.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Every sustained-history atom is identified by a proved product of observed at-risk transition kernels. The finite cell vector is estimated by cross-fitted longitudinal AIPW scores for intensive cell indicators and by numerator, survival-denominator, and ratio scores for the standard residual margin. Clipped, uniformly consistent backward-regression and censoring-hazard fits with \(o_{\mathsf P}(n^{-1/2})\) regression--censoring error products yield a root-\(n\) simultaneous rectangle on the quantitative submodel. Hall-feasible projection keeps its confidence polytope nonempty. Under pointwise overlap alone, the vanishing-information impossibility still applies.

prose_updates.related_work: JanvinRyalenSarvetStensrud2025 supplies the uncapped residual no-carry-over equality and threshold-wise scalar analysis. The cap-fibre construction here transfers sharpness after intersecting that class with \(B+W\le H\). Dahl2008 supplies the reindexed staircase feasibility criterion, and Hoffman1952 supplies only the fixed-matrix polyhedral error bound used for the new perspective-Lipschitz argument. BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 is used for the factual-arm sequential-CAR formulation and motivates longitudinal influence-function estimation; it does not assert identification of the entire sustained-history law. That law is derived here atom by atom from randomization, consistency, sequential CAR, and positivity, then specialized to \(r_{bt}\) and the numerator--denominator representation of \(q_w\). ChernozhukovHongTamer2007, AndrewsSoares2010, and Gafarov2025 motivate inference with binding inequalities and changing faces. The present positive result is a finite-dimensional conservative cross-fitted inversion under quantitative overlap, while the headline two-point theorem shows why the same conclusion is impossible uniformly under pointwise overlap. MontielOleaQiuStoye2026 motivates the decision relevance of the shared payoff set and randomization.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved scope includes exact endpoints, an observed-law-preserving raw-path causal lift, sharp transfer to the published raw no-carry-over subclass intersected with the cap, the complete common-law value set, deterministic and randomized minimax regret, and confidence-polytope inversion. Complete sustained-arm history identification is now proved directly by a finite observed-kernel product, rather than attributed to a source that identifies only particular functionals. Positive root-\(n\) margin, value-set, and regret-excess contraction holds only on the explicit quantitative inference regularity submodel with fixed \(H,K\), a fixed overlap lower bound, cross-fitting, clipped uniformly consistent nuisances, and longitudinal product-rate control. All deterministic and randomized ties retain simultaneous outer coverage. Geometric optimizer contraction is claimed only under an additional uniform deterministic regret gap or randomized polyhedral-sharpness inequality. On the unchanged pointwise-overlap class, uniformly honest regions need not shrink, as witnessed by the stated two-law sequences. SPRINT remains only a conditional capped-loss consumer requiring an externally defended cap at \(k=300\) and a feasible censoring-adjusted Hall system.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The cap \(H\) constrains only the separately capped summaries and never the primitive raw recurrent counts. Its clinical mechanism is not established for SPRINT. The response-tree lift preserves factual-arm sequential censoring without assuming censoring independence from the whole response tree. The positive inference theorem is not a consequence of the maintained class: it uses a separate quantitative predicate with uniform assignment, survival, and factual censoring overlap and explicit nuisance product rates. The conservative Bonferroni--Chebyshev rectangle establishes uniform root-\(n\) order but does not claim semiparametric efficiency or shortest width. At Hall and policy ties, outer coverage and regret-excess contraction remain valid, but optimizer-set distance need not contract without the displayed gap or polyhedral-sharpness condition. The broad-class impossibility sequences violate every fixed quantitative overlap bound and therefore do not contradict the positive submodel theorem.

statement_notes.justification: This lemma repairs the inferential foundation by deriving, rather than citing, the finite sequential factorization for every supported absorbing sustained-history atom.
statement_notes.gap: Published recurrent-event CAR results used here formulate the coarsening condition and identify particular mean or survival targets, not the complete history law needed for every capped terminal cell.
statement_notes.consumer: The explicit cell and ratio influence functions use the identified transition kernels to construct all backward outcome regressions.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem gives a computable positive inference result on exactly the quantitative submodel that excludes the headline vanishing-information sequences, and propagates root-\(n\) margin error through the transport geometry to values and decisions.
statement_notes.gap: Set-theoretic confidence inversion alone does not supply a first-stage construction, a contraction rate, or the regularity boundary under censoring; prior CAR and support-function literatures do not provide this capped recurrent-event composition.
statement_notes.consumer: A trial analysis satisfying prespecified quantitative overlap and cross-fitted nuisance-rate diagnostics can report one simultaneous region for all capped values and robust deterministic or randomized decisions, while retaining every tie.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem isolates the information-theoretic obstruction in the unchanged pointwise-overlap model by constructing total-variation-indistinguishable laws whose value sets or unique robust thresholds remain separated.
statement_notes.gap: Sequential CAR, pointwise positivity, and recurrent-event multiply robust estimation do not by themselves answer whether honest confidence regions can shrink uniformly when post-landmark observation probabilities approach zero.
statement_notes.consumer: Investigators must either verify a quantitative overlap and nuisance-rate submodel before using the positive cross-fitted result or report the broader-class nonshrinkage limitation; Hall slack and unique policies do not cure vanishing information.
